metadata.title: Memory Prices Hit Arm's Royalties as Stock Falls 4%

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM), which licenses the chip architecture behind most of the world's smartphones, fell 3.78% premarket despite beating on both lines. First-quarter revenue rose 22% to $1.29 billion against the $1.26 billion analysts expected, and non-GAAP earnings of $0.45 a share topped the $0.40 consensus.
Royalty revenue grew 22% to $715 million, with data center royalties more than doubling as Neoverse shipments passed 1.5 billion cores. Licensing revenue rose 23% to $574 million, free cash flow reached $665 million and non-GAAP operating margin widened 210 basis points to about 41.2%.
For the second quarter, management guided royalty growth of 13%, below what it had expected a couple of quarters earlier, pointing to smartphone weakness tied to higher memory prices, with higher licensing growth more than covering the shortfall. Total revenue is expected to come in at $1.38 billion give or take $50 million. Demand for its new AGI CPU now exceeds $2 billion across this fiscal year and next, double the $1 billion flagged a quarter ago, though management expects first-generation gross margins in the high 30% to low 40% range against a long-term target of 50%.
